cards.explanation: The answer is False. Paul says he is "…called to be an apostle of Christ Jesus by the will of God…" (1 Corinthians 1:1). Notice who does the calling there, friends. It isn't Paul sending in an application, it's God's will. Paul puts that right in the first line, before he says anything else.

The answer is holy. Paul says they are "…sanctified in Christ Jesus and called to be holy…" (1 Corinthians 1:2). Sanctified means set apart for God. He says it to the church in Corinth, in the very first lines of the letter. That's a big word for a greeting, friends, and he puts it right up front.

The answer is God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ. Paul writes, "Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ." (1 Corinthians 1:3). Paul and Sosthenes are the ones sending the letter, but they aren't the source of the grace. It comes from the Father and the Son, and that's a gift you can't bake yourself.

The answer is True. Paul says, "I always thank my God for you because of the grace He has given you in Christ Jesus." (1 Corinthians 1:4). His thanks goes to God, and the reason is the grace God has given them. It's the same word, grace, that he just used in his greeting. When a batch comes out right, I don't pat my own mustache on the back, and Paul doesn't pat the Corinthians on the back either.

The answer is in all speech and all knowledge. Paul says, "For in Him you have been enriched in every way, in all speech and all knowledge…" (1 Corinthians 1:5). Notice the "in Him" part, friends. This richness comes through Christ. It's the kind of wealth you can't count in a cookie jar.

The answer is spiritual. Paul says, "…you do not lack any spiritual gift…" (1 Corinthians 1:7). That's a strong thing to say to a church, friends. Not one spiritual gift missing. I wish my pantry could say that about sprinkles.

The answer is our Lord Jesus Christ. Paul says they eagerly await "…the revelation of our Lord Jesus Christ." (1 Corinthians 1:7). They have every spiritual gift, and still they're looking ahead to Him. That's why I keep my ovens ready, friends. I never claim to know when, only that I'm ready.

The answer is True. Paul says, "He will sustain you to the end, so that you will be blameless on the day of our Lord Jesus Christ." (1 Corinthians 1:8). Look at who does the sustaining, friends. It says "He will," so the holding up is His doing. I'd call that a very good deal.

The answer is faithful. Paul says, "God, who has called you into fellowship with His Son Jesus Christ our Lord, is faithful." (1 Corinthians 1:9). He ends the whole opening on that word, friends. After all those promises, it's what they can lean on.
